q: If two distinct non-zero real variables x and y are such that (x + y) is proportional to (x − y), then the value of x/y
options: depends on xy
depends only on x and not on y
depends only on y and not on x
is a constant
explanation: (x+y) = k(x−y) for some constant k gives x(1−k) = −y(1+k), so x/y = −(1+k)/(1−k), a fixed constant independent of the particular x, y, matching the official key (D).

q: Let L1, L2 be two regular languages and L3 a language which is not regular. Which of the following statements is/are always TRUE?
options: L1 = L2 if and only if L1 ∩ ¬L2 = ∅
L1 ∪ L3 is not regular
¬L3 is not regular
¬L1 ∪ ¬L2 is regular
explanation: Regular languages are closed under complement and union, so ¬L1 ∪ ¬L2 is always regular (D). The complement of a non-regular language is always non-regular, since regularity is closed under complement, so ¬L3 is not regular (C). Statement A only characterizes L1 ⊆ L2, not equality, and B fails whenever L1 already covers Σ* (e.g. L1 = Σ*), so L1 ∪ L3 can be regular, matching the official key (C, D).

q: Consider the circuit shown below where the gates may have propagation delays. Assume that all signal transitions occur instantaneously and that wires have no delays. Which of the following statements about the circuit is/are CORRECT?
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 160" width="100%" style="max-width:420px;height:auto" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="ah-2024s1cs28" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="6" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 Z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs><g fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"><text x="35" y="30" font-size="13" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">X</text><line x1="40" y1="40" x2="230" y2="40" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s1cs28)"/><line x1="55" y1="40" x2="55" y2="85"/><line x1="55" y1="85" x2="90" y2="85"/><path d="M90,70 L90,100 L130,85 Z" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s1cs28)"/><text x="98" y="90" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">NOT</text><circle cx="136" cy="85" r="4"/><line x1="140" y1="85" x2="180" y2="85"/><line x1="180" y1="85" x2="180" y2="70"/><line x1="180" y1="70" x2="230" y2="70" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s1cs28)"/><path d="M230,40 h30 a25,25 0 0 1 0,50 h-30 Z"/><text x="245" y="70" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">AND</text><line x1="285" y1="65" x2="310" y2="65" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s1cs28)"/><text x="295" y="55" font-size="13" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Y</text></g></svg>
options: With no propagation delays, the output Y is always logic Zero
With no propagation delays, the output Y is always logic One
With propagation delays, the output Y can have a transient logic One after X transitions from logic Zero to logic One
With propagation delays, the output Y can have a transient logic Zero after X transitions from logic One to logic Zero
explanation: Y = X AND (NOT X). With zero delay this is identically 0, so (A) holds. With a NOT-gate delay, when X rises from 0 to 1 the AND's direct input becomes 1 immediately while the NOT output (still reflecting the old X=0) briefly stays 1, so both AND inputs are momentarily 1, producing a transient logic One glitch, matching the official key (A, C). When X falls from 1 to 0 the direct input goes to 0 immediately, forcing Y to 0 with no glitch, so (D) is false.

q:
Consider the following two relations, R(A,B) and S(A,C):
R
A   B
10  20
20  30
30  40
30  50
50  95

S
A   C
10  90
30  45
40  80

The total number of tuples obtained by evaluating the following expression
σ(B<C) (R ⋈(R.A=S.A) S)
is ________
explanation: Joining on A gives (10,20,90), (30,40,45), (30,50,45) — the A=20 and A=50 rows of R and the A=40 row of S have no match. Applying B<C keeps (10,20,90) since 20<90 and (30,40,45) since 40<45, but drops (30,50,45) since 50≥45, leaving 2 tuples, matching the official key.

options: States 2 and 4 are distinguishable in M
States 3 and 4 are distinguishable in M
States 2 and 5 are distinguishable in M
Any string w with n0(w) = n1(w) is in L(M)
explanation: Transitions are 1→(2 on 0, 4 on 1), 2→(3 on 0, 1 on 1), 3→(1 on 0, 2 on 1), 4→(1 on 0, 5 on 1), 5→(4 on 0, 1 on 1), with state 1 the only accepting state. Partition refinement merges {2,5} and {3,4} into single equivalence classes, so states 3 and 4 are indistinguishable (making B false) and states 2 and 5 are indistinguishable (making C false), while 2 and 4 land in different classes and so are distinguishable (A true). The collapsed 3-state machine tracks (n0−n1) mod 3, and it accepts exactly when this is 0, which any w with n0(w)=n1(w) trivially satisfies, so D is also true. The officially keyed FALSE statements are B and C.
